mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous 3 months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high RSAFS growth periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a slowdown in economic activity, which typically leads to negative revisions in corporate earnings and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with subsequent negative earnings revisions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment that typically depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) are increasing, the combination signals a tight labor market with wage pressures, which typically leads to increased corporate costs and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low UNRATE and rising PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 3 months signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically boosts related sectors and positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high HOUST growth periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During an economic expansion, when GDP (GDPC1) growth is above 2% annualized and industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing, the combination signals robust economic activity that typically boosts corporate earnings and positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% annualized and INDPRO increasing
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of high GDPC1 growth and rising INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent positive earnings revisions.
